blindReviewDeclaration: Fresh falsification-first independent review. The current R5 design package, frozen upstream sources, corpus, standards and granularity controls were reviewed before the standalone round-1 review and intake. Independent findings and NO_GO were frozen before those two round-1 materials were read. No third Codex adversarial round is permitted.
expectedBehavior: 32 scenarios and 104 operations must be falsifiable in both directions, including the two deletions and one addition.
Every operation must have deterministic scenario, owner, page, security, query/request/response, status, idempotency, CAS, error and focused-test behavior.

The 12 units must preserve one deployable, seven owner modules, two independent apps, foundation-first UI, invitation-only assignment, internal-only ResolveNavigation, and one controlled r5-full business/cleanup proof.
Five extension value hosts, stable fixture keys/counts, secret references, exact remote allowlists, scenario prerequisites and controlled date boundaries must be executable without agent invention.

findings.title: 32↔104 remains only operation-to-scenario, not a normative reverse crosswalk
findings.evidence: The independent recount finds 104 unique operation rows and all 32 scenario IDs occur in operations[*].scenarioIds. The Journey decision has scenario rows and the catalog has operation rows, but neither provides a checked scenario-step→operationIds mapping with required operation completeness, two deletions, and one addition.
findings.risk: The denominator can be numerically green while a scenario is missing a required operation or an operation is orphaned; the development agent must infer the exact task contract from prose.
findings.disposition: CONFIRMED residual. Counterexample: a scenario can resolve one operation and still omit its required detail/readback/error operation. Minimal repair: add one checked 32-row scenarioOperationCrosswalk with ordered step IDs, operationIds, face, owner, page, disposition and positive/negative proof refs, and assert both-direction equality including deletedCandidates/addedOperations. Smaller than a traceability database; low-to-medium synchronization cost before implementation.
findings.counterexample: All 32 IDs are touched, but an omitted operation inside a scenario cannot be detected because no normative scenario-side operation set exists.
findings.minimalRepair: Add the checked reverse crosswalk and make the catalog checker compare both directions.
findings.largerAlternativeCost: A traceability database or Journey-by-Journey review is unnecessary; one versioned JSON crosswalk is smaller.

findings.title: Deleted page-guard semantics still survive in the normative component baseline
findings.evidence: catalog.componentFieldBaseline retains WorkspacePageEntryGuard and WorkspacePageEntryGuardRequest as Heritage refs, and also retains WorkspaceRoleCandidateCatalog after getWorkspaceRoleCandidates is deleted. componentOverrides.forbiddenProperties forbids workspaceKey/itemCodes/logoBindGrant but has no forbidden component/symbol closure. U06 correctly describes internal ResolveNavigation, but the baseline still gives a generated/component implementation path for the deleted guard contract.
findings.risk: A developer can regenerate or carry a page-guard DTO/component and recreate a second navigation/authorization truth while claiming compliance with the catalog; ResolveNavigation then ceases to be only internal UX readback.
findings.disposition: CONFIRMED residual. Counterexample: a generated client/component imports WorkspacePageEntryGuard because the baseline reference remains and no zero-reference rule rejects it. Minimal repair: remove the two page-guard refs and unused role-candidate ref from the selected component baseline, and add a checked forbiddenSymbols/zeroReference closure for deleted operation types and public ResolveNavigation exposure. Low cost; do not add a policy engine.
findings.counterexample: The deleted operation is absent from operations[], yet its request/response component references remain admissible in the generated component closure.
findings.minimalRepair: Delete the forbidden refs and add a negative symbol/reference assertion covering generated schemas, routes, tests and runtime.
findings.largerAlternativeCost: A generalized authorization policy engine is unnecessary and would expand scope.

findings.title: Operations extension-definition contract cannot select the required five value hosts
findings.evidence: r5-full defines five extensionDefinitions for BRAND, TENANT, HEAD_COMPANY, STORE and CONTRACT. The catalog has explicit entityType path binding for platform get/replaceExtensionDefinition, but getOperationsOrganizationBusinessEntityExtensionDefinition uses pageKey OPERATIONS-HEAD-COMPANY and only groupWorkspaceKey plus expectedContextVersion; it has no entityType/host discriminator. Other operations definition rows are separately hard-wired to stores or contracts, leaving the operations business-entity task unable to express the three entity hosts represented by the five-host requirement.
findings.risk: The developer must invent whether head-company is the only operations definition, whether one endpoint multiplexes hosts, or whether additional operations are needed; UI and owner readback can silently diverge from D-03.
findings.disposition: CONFIRMED residual. Counterexample: the same page can request a BRAND definition but the contract has no legal selector and the agent must add an unapproved query/path or hard-code HEAD_COMPANY. Minimal repair: choose one closed entityType enum on the operations business-entity definition operation (or explicitly add three operations), bind it to the five-host crosswalk and focused tests. The single closed enum is the smaller low-cost repair.
findings.counterexample: Five host fixtures exist, but the operations business-entity definition operation has no host selector and is named/anchored only for HEAD_COMPANY.
findings.minimalRepair: Add closed entityType semantics and crosswalk rows for BRAND/TENANT/HEAD_COMPANY, preserving separate STORE/CONTRACT owner endpoints.
findings.largerAlternativeCost: Adding a new endpoint per host is more expensive and risks unnecessary contract expansion.

findings.title: r5-full declares a generic prerequisite rule but no 32 scenario prerequisite fixtures
findings.evidence: scenarioPrerequisitePolicy contains denominator 32 and a mapping source to operations[*].scenarioIds, plus a generic rule. It does not contain 32 concrete scenario rows with positive fixture refs and declared negative/stale/denied/disabled refs. businessPassPredicates asserts that all sets resolve, but those sets are not present in the contract.
findings.risk: Seed and acceptance agents still decide at runtime which fixtures prove each scenario and negative branch; stable counts alone cannot prove business coverage.
findings.disposition: CONFIRMED residual. Counterexample: two scenarios can resolve the same generic workspace fixture and pass the predicate while the required invitation, stale context or contract-date branch is absent. Minimal repair: add explicit 32-row prerequisite entries and negative refs, reusing existing stable keys. Low fixture-manifest cost.
findings.counterexample: The predicate names prerequisite sets that are not represented as data in r5-full.
findings.minimalRepair: Freeze positiveFixtureRefs and negativeFixtureRefs for every scenario before seed implementation.
findings.largerAlternativeCost: A generalized scenario data service is unnecessary.

findings.title: Platform credential fixtures do not carry complete secret references
findings.evidence: profile.credentialSources lists source names, and pa-bootstrap has passwordSource, but pa-support and pa-disabled only declare createPlatformAdmin channels with no credentialSource/secretRef. Recovery, invitation, reset and session credential purposes likewise have no per-fixture secret reference or purpose binding.
findings.risk: The agent must choose how stable platform accounts and recovery flows obtain credentials, which can create undocumented defaults or make the acceptance run non-reproducible.
findings.disposition: CONFIRMED residual. Counterexample: pa-support is expected to log in but its fixture row has no password source, so implementation can silently reuse the bootstrap secret or invent a local default. Minimal repair: add non-secret secretRef/purpose fields for every credential-bearing fixture and recovery/OTP grant; keep values external and forbidden from persistence/logs. Low cost.
findings.counterexample: A stable account without a credentialSource cannot be deterministically exercised.
findings.minimalRepair: Add secretRef and purpose to all platform/operations/recovery fixture rows without adding secret values.
findings.largerAlternativeCost: A credential service is out of scope; source references are sufficient.

findings.title: Reset fail-closed wording refers to an undefined exact remote allowlist
findings.evidence: r5-full names V2S_DEV_REMOTE_HOST, databaseUrlSource, namespace pattern and assetRootSource, and resetFailClosedPredicates says host/database/schema/asset root must be in an explicit DEV allowlist. The contract does not freeze the allowed host set, database/schema rule, or asset-root prefix/namespace mapping.
findings.risk: A reset runner can satisfy the prose with different host or path checks, weakening destructive-operation isolation and making cleanup evidence incomparable.
findings.disposition: CONFIRMED residual. Counterexample: two runners accept different remote hosts or schema patterns while both report the generic allowlist predicate PASS. Minimal repair: add exact allowlist identifiers/patterns and namespace-to-database/schema/asset-root derivation to r5-full, with a negative matrix. Low cost and no dynamic run required.
findings.counterexample: The phrase explicit DEV allowlist is a requirement but no exact allowlist data is supplied.
findings.minimalRepair: Freeze exact remote host, database, schema and asset root allowlist predicates and their negative fixtures.
findings.largerAlternativeCost: A generalized environment policy service is unnecessary.

findings.title: Contract date profiles are symbolic rather than bound to controlled clock values
findings.evidence: stableFixtures.contracts use dateProfile values CURRENT, FUTURE, PAST and ENDED, while the blueprint and U07 require controlled-date three-state derivation. No exact controlled clock instants or date endpoints are specified in r5-full, so the same fixture can change state with the run date or an implementation-defined offset.
findings.risk: OPERATING/PREPARING/NOT_OPERATING and invalid/ended negative evidence can drift or differ between agents while expectedCounts remain green.
findings.disposition: CONFIRMED residual. Counterexample: a FUTURE contract becomes CURRENT if the runner chooses today differently, or PAST/ENDED boundaries differ by timezone. Minimal repair: bind each dateProfile to explicit UTC instants and a controlled BusinessDateProvider readback, including boundary cases. Low test-fixture cost.
findings.counterexample: Symbolic CURRENT/FUTURE/PAST/ENDED labels do not determine actual interval comparisons.
findings.minimalRepair: Add exact effective/expiry timestamps and fixed clock profiles to r5-full.
findings.largerAlternativeCost: A production scheduling abstraction is unnecessary for DEV proof.

solutionReasonableness.problemFit: The selected one-deployable, owner-command, generated-face and carry-over-first design fits the approved 32-scenario problem; the remaining gaps are closure defects in that design, not a reason to expand topology.
solutionReasonableness.simplerAlternativeAssessment: The smaller repairs are checked reverse crosswalk rows, forbidden component references, one closed host discriminator, explicit fixture rows, secret refs, allowlist predicates and fixed clock values; splitting R5 or adding a platform is less reasonable.
solutionReasonableness.costFit: The repair cost is bounded and materially lower than letting implementation invent behavior and discovering it in business verification.

conclusion.summary: R5 DESIGN round 2 is NO_GO. Independent residual findings are 3 M / 4 S / 0 N: the catalog is now per-operation and the round-1 defects are largely closed, but reverse scenario trace, deleted component closure, operations five-host contract selection, and deterministic fixture details are not fully frozen.
conclusion.authorizationBoundary: Design review only. No implementation, production-source modification, DEV, remote, seed, reset, dynamic business run, or repository-control action is authorized. Round 2 is final; no third Codex adversarial round.
